halves.sub: N+1 per-row conversation count on the report user-breakdown listing
halves.message: Read per-user conversation counts from the association in the report breakdown
halves.exact_change: `conversations_count: row["conversations_count"].to_i` -> `conversations_count: Conversation.where(user_id: row["user_id"]).count`. The CTE (conversation_counts) still runs and still SELECTs conversations_count, but the row map now IGNORES that grouped alias and issues one `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversations WHERE user_id = ?` per rendered row -> 1+N on the user-breakdown listing (up to USER_LIMIT=100 extra COUNT queries per page).
halves.routed_path_evidence: Admin::Report#user_breakdown (report.rb:53-113) builds the per-user listing; it is the aggregator's only per-row grouped-count listing. (Admin::ReportsController#index:6 calls @report.user_breakdown(page:), but the controller/feature is unrouted and unviewed — see structural findings — so exposure is through the Admin::Report API, not HTTP.) Value is identical (CTE conversation_count == per-row COUNT), so it is a pure performance regression.
halves.stays_green: No report test exists and no query-count guard anywhere in the suite; the only system test is admin_users (admin USER management), which never hits Admin::Report. Value unchanged. Suite stays GREEN; app boots (ruby -c OK).
halves.adaptation: GLM/deepseek #7a flipped a grouped/cached count to `.count` on a rendered LIST partial. Nex has no reports view and the admin USER list renders NO per-row count, so the equivalent 'single grouped query -> per-row .count' lives in the aggregator's own per-row listing (user_breakdown). Faithful 'grouped query still runs, row ignores the alias and issues a per-row COUNT' (GLM #7a precedent), same class (N+1), same Med 2. One field flipped (minimal), mirroring the single-field parity change.
halves.parity_reference: Med 2, same class/mechanism as glm_5_3_full_b300 #7a (grouped alias -> user.conversations.count on the admin user list) and deepseek_v4_1_flash_b300 #7a (counter_cache column -> conversation.messages.count on the conversation list).

halves.exact_change: New migration: `remove_index :messages, name: "index_messages_on_created_at_and_id"` + `add_index :messages, [:role, :created_at], name: "index_messages_on_role_and_created_at"`. Drops the sprint-4 messages [created_at, id] reporting index (added in 20261020160000_add_reporting_indexes) and replaces it with a leading-role composite.
halves.target_query: The dropped [created_at, id] index backed Admin::Report#activity -> activity_counts(Message) (report.rb:169-183: `date_trunc('day', messages.created_at)` GROUP BY + ORDER BY, NO role predicate) and the summary window filter `timestamp_scope(Message)` (where created_at in window_range). The new [role, created_at] composite leads with role, so it cannot serve the no-role created_at range/group scan; the surviving [conversation_id, created_at, id] composite (index_messages_on_conversation_and_activity, from the create_chat_domain migration) leads with conversation_id and also cannot. Message activity rollup now full-scans.

ADAPTATION: Nex tracks NO db/schema.rb, so this is a migration-only edit with no schema.rb sync (the parity refs synced schema.rb). The dropped index is Nex's sprint-4 `add_reporting_indexes` messages index (not a create_chat_domain index), matching 'drop one of the indexes that backs a reports rollup'. messages has a real `role` column (create_chat_domain migration), so the false composite is valid.

items.name: silently wrong aggregate — report message total counts only ACTIVE users' messages
items.message: Scope the reporting message total to active accounts
items.exact_change: `messages_count: timestamp_scope(Message).count` -> `messages_count: timestamp_scope(Message).joins(conversation: :user).merge(User.active).count`. The window message-total now EXCLUDES messages belonging to deactivated users' conversations. The sibling `conversations_count` (line 46) is left on the full set, so the two headline totals silently disagree.
items.routed_path_evidence: Admin::Report#summary (report.rb:41-51) is the dashboard summary object (@summary in Admin::ReportsController#index:5). The messages_count figure is the platform-wide message total for the selected window; it must count ALL messages, not only active users'. Once any user is deactivated (active_users < total_users) with messages in the window, the figure silently under-reports engagement. Ground truth != reported.
items.wrongness: A platform message-volume metric scoped to active accounts under-reports every time a deactivated user has messages in the window; the empty/all-active case matches, so it reads as a reasonable 'exclude deactivated noise' tweak while being wrong for the stated metric.
items.stays_green: No report test exists (no pin on summary.messages_count), so GREEN trivially; additionally the join/merge is value-identical whenever all users are active. ruby -c = Syntax OK. App boots.
items.adaptation: deepseek_v4_1_flash_b300 #8 narrowed admins_count (admin -> admin AND active); glm_5_3_full_b300 #8 narrowed the per-user message AVERAGE denominator (total_users -> active_users). Nex's summary has no admins figure and no average, so the same 'narrow a total to ACTIVE so it matches all-active fixtures but diverges under deactivation' pattern is applied to the headline messages total. Same class (silently wrong aggregate), same Med 2. Disjoint from #7a by METHOD+LINE (summary:47 vs user_breakdown map:100) and by CLASS (correctness vs performance); they share report.rb only because Nex folded all report logic into one 185-line object with no view (recorded).
items.parity_reference: Med 2, same class (green-but-wrong active-narrowed count) as deepseek_v4_1_flash_b300 #8 and glm_5_3_full_b300 #8.
items.fix: restore messages_count to timestamp_scope(Message).count (the full window total)
